How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. pages.text: How To Find Dinosaur Bones | National Geographic TRAVEL DIGITAL NOMAD How To Find Dinosaur Bones By Andrew Evans Published July 29, 2013 • 7 min read Though I travel far and wide, it is rare that I get to travel so far back in time (to the Cretaceous period) and walk among the gigantic wildlife (dinosaurs) who once romped along the tropical shores of central Montana . Admittedly, I was once a young boy with a bedroom full of plastic dinosaurs and an obsession with beasts for which there was no zoo, and traveling to Montana turned me back into that very same kid, giddy with the thrill of hunting down any vague remnant of the prehistoric past. Now, finding dinosaur bones is hard work , and not as simple or quick as the movies might indicate, but just an hour after heading out from the Two Medicine Dinosaur Center , I had already spotted and correctly identified my first real dinosaur bone fragment. I spent the rest of the day digging in the dirt, imagining the Hadrosaurid and Ceratopsian melee that took place on this very spot. One day on a dig does not a paleontologist make, but in the time I spent searching for dinosaurs, I sure learned a lot—like how I lack the patience it takes to be a paleontologist but how awesome it would be. I also learned the seven fundamental steps behind finding dinosaur bones: 1. Your report to the FDA is important. Thank you for submitting it. The FDA continues to devote time, energy, and resources to monitor reports of illness that could be related to pet foods, to determine their root causes where possible. The FDA will review your report to determine whether any follow-up investigation is possible or needed based on the information provided. A follow-up investigation could include collecting pet food or treats, or seeking a diagnostic sample from your pet for analysis. Even if no testing of pet food products or diagnostic samples is needed, your report will be part of adverse event and product problem surveillance to help prevent future problems. You may choose to have your pet food product tested by a private laboratory, but testing may be costly. The FDA cannot pay for private laboratory testing costs or provide reimbursement for veterinary costs associated with your animal’s illness. pages.title: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: John Holmes and his wife explain why they have returned to Ukraine after initially fleeing.
pages.text: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'Friends think we're idiots for returning to Ukraine' 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kevin Shoesmith East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire John Holmes Liliya Holmes and her British husband John pictured in Odesa, Ukraine When Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, John Holmes – a British national – and his Ukrainian wife Liliya fled the port city of Odesa, fearing for their lives. But after four years in the UK, the draw of home has proven too strong and they have returned to Ukraine's third largest city, undeterred by the sustained threat of air raids. "Friends of ours thought we were idiots for going back to Ukraine," reflects John, 74. "But returning is something we felt we needed to do. "Yes, it's dangerous. Yes, there are drones flying overhead. Yes, you can hear the explosions. But you just have to get on with life as best you can. "Home is Ukraine." During their time away, the pair sought sanctuary in Hull , East Yorkshire, where John was born and raised and has a property. He met Liliya, 64, in Ukraine and had been living there for 30 years until the invasion. "We had built a good life here," he says. pages.text: In this Canadian province grown-ups can dig up dinosaur fossils | National Geographic TRAVEL In this Canadian province grown-ups can dig up dinosaur fossils Dinosaur stories are often written for children, with a cast of neon cartoon characters or animatronic models. But for adults who never outgrew their fossil fascination, the Canadian province of Alberta offers a chance to explore the truth behind the fiction, witness new discoveries and touch real dinosaur bones with your bare hands. Close to 50 dinosaur species have been found in Alberta, including Albertosaurus, a formidable predator related to Tyrannosaurus rex . Photograph by Bella Falk By Bella Falk Published October 10, 2025 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). This journey back in time starts in southern Alberta, two hours east of Calgary, where the ground cracks open to reveal a prehistoric archive dating back some 76 million years. Here, the rolling prairie collapses into wrinkled valleys carved out by ancient glaciers, banded in orange and grey layers like the pages of a medieval book and punctuated by bizarre ‘hoodoos’ — pillars of rock wearing jaunty sandstone hats. These are Canada’s Badlands — so-called because early French fur traders found them inhospitable and difficult to cross. In this treeless desert, only the hardiest vegetation survives: yellow buffalo bean flowers and tiny pincushion cacti sprout between gullies, and the aroma of sagebrush hangs on the breeze. I maintain a map of vending machines built from OpenStreetMap data, part of a site that connects vending operators with venues (link at the end). It covers France, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Italy and is refreshed every month from Geofabrik extracts. While importing the 8 November 2026 extract, a few things about how vending machines are tagged stood out. I’m sharing them in case they are useful to mappers and data consumers. The numbers. The French extracts (mainland and overseas) contain 37,259 objects tagged amenity=vending_machine . The map shows 7,779 of them: those whose vending=* value (or, failing that, name ) is a product people seek out, such as food, drinks, bread, pizza, farm products, hygiene products and food lockers. Left out are, among others, machines with no identifiable product, cigarette machines and parcel lockers. The figures below refer to these 7,779 machines, compared with 17,924 selected the same way in Germany. Product mix. The most common values are condoms (1,456), pizza (1,425) and bread (934). Germany, with more than twice as many machines on the map, has 132 pizza and 42 bread machines. One machine, several products. In France, 1,530 machines (20%) list several products in a single semicolon-separated value, in no fixed order: drinks;sweets 418 times, sweets;drink

pages.text: Inside Paul Sereno's dinosaur hunt through the world’s fiercest desert | National Geographic By Paul Sereno Photographs by Keith Ladzinski Published July 15, 2025 As the Saharan sun rose on my waylaid team, one morning in September 2022, it seemed to burn with particular intensity. For nearly three weeks we’d been holed up in a mud-walled compound in the oasis town of Agadez, in central Niger, stalled because of officials’ insistence on assembling for us a large armed escort. Now, as dawn broke, we were finally ready to embark: Nearly a hundred people packed into 15 vehicles, a motley caravan of SUVs, pickups, and one large dump truck, all strapped with sand ladders and spare tires, heading out on an extraordinary desert dinosaur hunt—without question, the most ambitious of my career. pages.text: Inside the making of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi | National Geographic By Richard Conniff Photographs by Craig Cutler Published July 2, 2026 Dinosaurs are winging in at 550 miles an hour from across the planet: Diplodocus , Stegosaurus, a herd of Triceratops , and a pair of Tyrannosaurus rex (plus a carcass for the tyrannosaurs to do combat over). The museum has them in a queue, along with thousands of other specimens, from a fog-basking beetle to a reconstructed dodo. Some of them are awaiting takeoff, and some are in flight. Others are being uncrated, condition-checked, 3D-scanned, and quickly moved out for reassembly on the museum floor, all to make room for the next specimens just rolling through the delivery bay door. It’s early November 2025, and there are 20 days left until the opening of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi (NHMAD), a 377,000-square-foot structure being built and populated on what even the museum’s managers admit is an “insanely short” five-year timeline. With luck, the final major specimen—the last of five 75-foot-tall sauropods greeting visitors at the entrance—will arrive in time to go on display a day or two before the soft opening. That’s when Abu Dhabi’s royal families will arrive, fully expecting to be impressed. At the moment, however, that dinosaur, a Diplodocus, is still in Canada. And the mount is not yet complete. pages.description: A proposed class action says Intel hid the impact of slowing sales, inflating its shares.
pages.text: Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge 7 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Osmond Chia Business reporter Bloomberg via Getty Images Intel boss Tan Lip-Bu Shareholders have sued US chip giant Intel, accusing it of hiding the severity of a slump in personal computer (PC) sales, which they say led to a nearly 29% one-day collapse in the firm's stock. A proposed class action lawsuit in San Jose, California said Intel was too late to alert shareholders about how slowing sales could impact its earnings, allegedly artificially inflating its stock price. Intel shares plunged on 30 October, erasing tens of billions of dollars off its market value the day after it forecasted disappointing revenue in its coming earnings report. The BBC has contacted Intel for comment. The lawsuit, filed by legal firm Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd on behalf of owners of Intel common shares between 23 July and 29 October this year, was filed against the chipmaker, its chief executive Tan Lip-Bu and other company leaders. Intel has been accused of making "materially false and/or misleading" statements that failed to disclose the slowdown in PC sales and the impact of its data centre projects, the complaint said. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Considered an "Enemy Race" in Their Own Country This is how Western Defense Commander John L. DeWitt characterized people of Japanese ancestry during World War II. He insisted that even those who had been born and raised as U.S. citizens nevertheless posed a threat because their Japanese “racial strains” were “undiluted.” Under the authority of President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Executive Order 9066, DeWitt ordered the removal of all Japanese Americans from the West Coast in 1942. Allowed to take only what they could carry, they were imprisoned, without trial, in some of the most desolate places in the country. Today, the National Park Service preserves those sites so that visitors may learn their story. Close jfd553's Diary Mapping Icefields Parkway, Part 1: A two-year mapping journey Posted by jfd553 on 4 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 6 November 2026. I spent two years mapping the areas surrounding one of the most beautiful drives in the world. Each morning, I looked forward to discovering and mapping an area adjacent to a one I did the day before. This diary entry serves as an introduction to a series of texts covering the challenges I encountered and how I overcame them. Included below are a few snapshots taken in the field, which capture the majestic landscapes along the Icefields Parkway. I have also added a “before and after” map excerpt, as well as a short video, to illustrate how my work gradually took shape over time. The Place The Icefields Parkway (Highway 93N), in Alberta, owes its name to the spectacular icefields and glaciers that line the road. The parkway, which is a 232 km stretch of highway cutting through Banff and Jasper National Parks, attracts between 1.2 million and 2 million visitors per year. The parkway offers exceptional alpine landscape, with glaciers, rivers, turquoise lakes, and breathtaking mountain views directly from the roadside (Figure 1). Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn K2-Play Completes Final Phase of North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan Oct 15, 2026 FRUITA, Colo. – Over the past eight years, the North Fruita Desert has changed in ways riders can see as soon as they arrive. There are more miles of singletrack, more places to camp and dedicated space for races and other large events, all part of a broader effort by the Bureau of Land Management and community partners to keep pace with one of western Colorado’s busiest recreation areas. This fall, the final trail in the North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan is complete. K2-Play winds for about three miles along the base of the Book Cliffs and completes the final phase of a roughly 30-mile expansion of the 18 Road trail system. Its completion caps years of planning and construction involving the BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Colorado Plateau Mountain Bike Trail Association, Mesa County, City of Fruita, local businesses, professional trail builders and volunteers. Katmai, parque nacional y reserva desde 1980, aún es famoso por sus volcanes, pero también por sus osos pardos, sus prístinos cursos de agua con abundancia de peces, su vida silvestre remota y su litoral irregular. Planifique su visita El Parque Nacional y Reserva Katmai se extiende sobre casi 5 millones de acres (2 millones de ha) de un campo remoto espectacular. Los volcanes glaciales y los desolados escombros volcánicos se elevan por encima de los acantilados escarpados y los densos matorrales de alisos. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Protecting Lands and Giving Back to Communities The Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) was established by Congress in 1964 to fulfill a bipartisan commitment to safeguard our natural areas, water resources and cultural heritage, and to provide recreation opportunities to all Americans. Using zero taxpayer dollars, the LWCF invests earnings from offshore oil and gas leasing to help strengthen communities, preserve our history and protect our national endowment of lands and waters. The LWCF program is divided into the " State Side " which provides grants to State and local governments, and the " Federal Side " which is used to acquire lands, waters, and interests therein necessary to achieve the natural, cultural, wildlife, and recreation management objectives of federal land management agencies. The Land and Water Conservation Fund was permanently reauthorized in the Dingell Act of March 2019 and in August 2020 the Great American Outdoors Act fully and permanently funded the program.
